subject.title: fix(agents): protect provider auth exchange output by sensitivity, not input marker

question: After real implicit-Mantle proof is added, does the auth/secrets owner approve output-based classification as the canonical sentinel boundary for every provider runtime-auth hook?
rationale: This changes a shared credential-classification boundary and expands sentinel handling beyond SecretRef-marked inputs, so security ownership and intent cannot be settled by green CI alone.

options.title: Require live proof and approve
options.body: Require a redacted ambient-AWS Mantle run covering token minting through successful provider egress, then approve the shared output-based boundary.

options.title: Accept seam proof
options.body: Accept the injected token-provider evidence as sufficient and approve after source-only sibling-provider review.

options.title: Narrow the patch
options.body: Limit protection to Mantle-specific output, accepting duplicated provider policy and weaker recurrence prevention.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and approve
recommendation.body: Require a redacted ambient-AWS Mantle run covering token minting through successful provider egress, then approve the shared output-based boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the sentinel egress boundary and its security hardening, making them the strongest available individual routing candidate alongside the CODEOWNERS security team.
